issue_context.title: Command line sensor warns about needing `device_class` set with temperature `unit_of_measurement` but does not support it
issue_context.body:
### The problem

It appears that command line sensors don't support the device_class tag and is throwing a warning about needing them for temperature values.  Adding the device class to the customize.yaml also doesn't fix the warning.  

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2021.9.7

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Command Line Sensor

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor.command_line/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
configuration.yaml

    - platform: command_line
      name: cpu_0_temperature
      command: cat /config/cpu0temp.txt
      unit_of_measurement: "°C"
    
    - platform: command_line
      name: P8J8XDVR_Temperature
      command: cat /config/P8J8XDVRtemp.txt
      unit_of_measurement: "°C"

    - platform: command_line
      name: 200703809989_Temperature
      command: cat /config/200703809989temp.txt
      unit_of_measurement: "°C"

    - platform: command_line
      name: P8G1G7YR_Temperature
      command: cat /config/P8G1G7YRtemp.txt
      unit_of_measurement: "°C"

    - platform: command_line
      name: ST4000VN008_Temperature
      command: cat /config/ST4000VN008temp.txt
      unit_of_measurement: "°C"
```

customize.yaml
```yaml
sensor.cpu_0_temperature:
  friendly_name: CPU temperature
  device_class: temperature
sensor.p8g1g7yr_temperature:
  device_class: temperature
sensor.st4000vn008_temperature:
  device_class: temperature
sensor.p8j8xdvr_temperature:
  device_class: temperature
sensor.200703809989_temperature:
  device_class: temperature
```



### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt

Please update your configuration if device_class is manually configured, otherwise create a bug report at https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3A%22integration%3A+command_line%22

I just stumbled upon this bug/feature request cause I have a command line sensor that runs an external script to gather the amount of energy used to charge the car. I want that to have that information as an individual device in the Energy panel, but that only works when both `device_class` and `state_class` are set, and the command line sensor doesn't accept that in its configuration.

Pull request https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/61506 looks straight forward enough to be used as a reference for a PR to add the `state_class`, but because of some technicalities that pull request was never merged.

So... because of those technicalities the only workaround is to create a template sensor that reflects the state and attributes of the command line sensor while adding `device_class` and `state_class` attributes, correct? In my opinion the changes required to the command line sensor up to date are so minimal (7 trivial additions for the `device_class` plus some lines for the tests) they clearly outweigh the requirements for a full rewrite of this sensor.

review_comments:
So there is an issue with this, this PR violates ADR-0007 at this point.

We no longer allow integrations to add or change a platform YAML configuration.

More information on this can be found in Architecture Decision Record:

- ADR-0007: <https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/blob/master/adr/0007-integration-config-yaml-structure.md#decision>

So this would take it from a minor change to a breaking change.  I feel like it would be best to break it all the way and change it so that the configuration would be done with the GUI.  It would be a lot more work, and there are still plenty of things that I don't have a full grasp on for making that large of a change, but it would save from having two breaking changes down the line.  

Is there a preference for which route to take?
It looks like #63840 would solve the ADR-0007 issue and the code appears mostly compatible.  The main change is the `def setup_platform` --> `async def async_setup_platform` section.
